cards.title: Open the Command Bar
questions: how do i open the command bar
how do i type a url
steps: Click New Tab in the sidebar, or press Command-T.
Type an address, a search, or the name of a tab, setting or command.
Press Return.

cards.title: Ask Ode how to do something
steps: Open the Command Bar, type help or ode, and press Tab. Or type ? and a space.
Ask your question, such as how do I split view.
Press Return to run Do It, or press Tab first to read the guide instead.
cards.note: You can also type a question straight into the Command Bar. When one answer fits, it shows first.

cards.title: Change the address of the current tab
questions: change the url of this tab
copy the address of this page
go to a different site in this tab
steps: Click the address at the top of the sidebar, or press Command-L.
Type a new address or search.
Press Return to open it in the same tab.

cards.title: Search the web
steps: Open the Command Bar.
Type what you're looking for.
Press Return. Ode searches with the search engine your Space uses.

cards.title: Go straight to the top result of a search
questions: go directly to the first result
steps: Type a search in the Command Bar.
Press Shift-Return. The tab goes straight to the search's first result instead of the results page.
On a site, tab or history row, Shift-Return still opens it in Split View. The selected row says which.
cards.note: Ode finds the result with DuckDuckGo, or Kagi when it's your Space's search engine, and sends your search only when you press Shift-Return. It works in a Quick Window too. Offline, Shift-Return opens the results as Return does.

cards.title: Search YouTube, Wikipedia or another site from the Command Bar
questions: search youtube from the command bar
how do i search wikipedia directly
steps: Open the Command Bar and type a site's shortcut, such as yt for YouTube or w for Wikipedia.
Press Tab. The site's name appears beside the field.
Type your search and press Return.
cards.note: You can also type $ and the shortcut, then a space, such as $yt.

cards.title: Ask ChatGPT, Claude or Perplexity from the Command Bar
questions: ask chatgpt from the command bar
ask ai from the address bar
steps: Open the Command Bar and type the assistant's name, such as chatgpt, claude or perplexity.
Press Tab.
Type your question and press Return. It opens on the assistant's own site.
cards.note: Ode only opens the assistant's website. It sends nothing to it by itself.

cards.title: Change your default search engine
questions: how do i change the search engine
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Search.
Under Default search, pick a search engine or an AI assistant.
A Space can use its own engine: pick it under Search with on the Space's Browsing page.

cards.title: Add your own search engine or site search
questions: add search engine with url template
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Search.
Click Add Provider…, then enter a name, a shortcut and the search address with %s where the search words go.
Click Save. Type the shortcut in the Command Bar and press Tab to use it.
cards.note: Search addresses must use HTTPS.

cards.title: Change or turn off a site search shortcut
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Search.
Click a provider to change its shortcuts and options, or turn it off.
To undo your changes, click Restore Defaults. Providers you added stay.

cards.title: Find an open tab
questions: switch to a tab by name
where is that tab i had open
steps: Open the Command Bar.
Type part of the tab's title or address. Open tabs show first.
Press Return to switch to it. Type @tabs and a space to see only tabs.

cards.title: Search only tabs, history, saved tabs, actions or Spaces
questions: only show tabs in command bar
steps: Open the Command Bar.
Type @tabs, @history, @saved, @actions or @spaces, then a space or Tab.
Type your search. Press Escape to leave the filter and keep your text.

cards.title: Run a command or open a setting by typing its name
questions: run a command from the command bar
open settings from the command bar
steps: Open the Command Bar.
Type what you want to do, such as archive, downloads, split or reader. Settings pages show too.
Press Return to run it. Initials work as well, such as tsv for Toggle Split View.

cards.title: Do quick math in the Command Bar
questions: do math in the address bar
can the command bar do sums
steps: Open the Command Bar.
Type a sum, such as 24 * 7. The answer shows below the search.
Select the answer and press Return to copy it.

cards.title: Convert units and check the time somewhere else
questions: convert units in the command bar
what time is it in another city
steps: Type a conversion, such as 5 km in miles or how many ounces in a pound.
Or type time in and a place, such as time in Tokyo, or a time to convert, such as 3pm New York in London.
The answer shows below the search. Press Down, then Return to copy it.
cards.note: Conversions and times are worked out on your Mac, so nothing is sent. Turn them off with Conversions under Also show in Settings > Search.

cards.title: Look up a word in the dictionary
questions: how do i find what a word means
steps: Type define and the word, such as define ephemeral, or just the word.
The Mac's definition shows below the search. Press Down, then Return to open it in Dictionary.
cards.note: The definition comes from your Mac, so nothing is sent. A Mac that has never used its dictionary downloads it first, and definitions show once it's ready.

cards.title: Show Wikipedia summaries in the Command Bar
questions: info card about a person or place
why does a wikipedia card show up
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Search.
Under Also show, turn on Web Answers.
Type a topic's exact name, such as Albert Einstein. A summary shows below the search, and Return opens the article.
cards.note: It's off until you turn it on. Then what you type goes to Wikipedia, never in a private window. Pictures show only when they're freely licensed, with their author and licence.

cards.title: Open a link you just copied
questions: paste a link and open it
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click Search, and turn on Paste and Go under Also show.
Copy a link in any app, then open the Command Bar. The link shows as the first result.
Press Return to open it.
cards.note: Paste and Go is off until you turn it on.

cards.title: Open a Command Bar result in a new tab, Split View or Quick Window
questions: open in new tab from command bar
steps: Select a result in the Command Bar.
Hold Command for a background tab, Shift-Command for a new tab, Shift for Split View, or Option for a Quick Window.
Press Return while you hold the keys.
cards.note: On a search, Shift opens the search's first result instead of Split View.

cards.title: Change what the Command Bar shows
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Search.
Under Results, choose Blended or sections, Top Hit and Show match reasons.
Under Sections, turn kinds of results on or off and drag them into the order you want.

cards.title: Make the Command Bar forget what it learned
questions: command bar keeps suggesting the wrong site
remove a suggestion from the command bar
steps: To forget one result, select it in the Command Bar and press Shift-Delete.
To forget everything, choose Ode > Settings, click Search, then click Clear Learned Choices.
To stop learning, turn off Learn from my choices.
cards.note: What the Command Bar learns stays on this Mac and is never learned in a private window.

cards.title: Turn off search suggestions
questions: stop sending what i type to google
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Search.
Turn off Search suggestions under Default search.
A Space with its own search engine has its own switch on its Browsing page.
cards.note: Suggestions send what you type to the search engine. Private windows never fetch them, and Ode never sends an address you typed, text that looks like a password, key or card number, or text a tab or your history already answers.

cards.title: Hide AI answers in Google and other search results
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Search.
Click your search engine in the list of providers.
Turn on its option, such as Hide AI Overviews for Google.

cards.title: What pinned, saved and open tabs are
questions: what is the difference between pinned and saved tabs
what is the line in the sidebar
why are some tabs above the line
pinned vs saved vs open tabs
steps: Pinned tabs are the icons at the top, for sites you use every day.
Saved tabs sit above the line and stay until you delete them.
Open tabs sit below the line and move to Archive when you clear them or after a while.

cards.title: Close a tab
questions: how do i close this tab
steps: Press Command-W, or right-click the tab in the sidebar and choose Close Tab.
An open tab goes to Archive, so you can bring it back.
Closing a pinned or saved tab only puts its page away. The tab stays in the sidebar.

cards.title: Reopen a tab you closed
questions: bring back a tab i closed
i closed a tab by accident
get back the tab i just closed
steps: Choose Tabs > Reopen Closed Tab.
Do it again to bring back the tab you closed before that.
For older tabs, open Archive and click the one you want.

cards.title: Archive a tab
questions: put this tab in the archive
steps: Show the open tab you want to archive.
Choose Tabs > Archive Tab. The tab leaves the sidebar and waits in Archive.
cards.note: Archive Tab works on open tabs. Pinned and saved tabs stay in the sidebar.

cards.title: Clear all open tabs at once
steps: Choose Tabs > Clear Unpinned Tabs, or move the pointer over the sidebar and click Clear on the line above your open tabs.
Every open tab in this Space moves to Archive. Pinned and saved tabs, and other Spaces, stay.
To bring them all back in their order, choose Tabs > Reopen Closed Tab right after, or open Archive.

cards.title: Archive old open tabs now
steps: Click ••• beside the Space's name and choose Clean Up Current Tabs.
Open tabs you haven't used for longer than each Space's archive time move to Archive.
cards.note: It works in every Space, and skips tabs that are showing or playing sound. To clear every open tab in this Space, choose Tabs > Clear Unpinned Tabs.

cards.title: Change when open tabs archive themselves
questions: stop tabs from closing by themselves
why did my tabs disappear after 12 hours
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click your Space in the sidebar and click Browsing.
Under Archive current tabs, choose After 12 Hours, After 24 Hours, After 7 Days, After 30 Days or Never.
Click Archive Now to run it right away.
cards.note: Each Space has its own setting. New Spaces archive after 12 hours.

cards.title: Sort open tabs into folders automatically
steps: In Settings > Search > Tab organization, turn on Enable suggestions and pick a Tab organization model.
Move the pointer over the sidebar and click Tidy on the line.
Check the folders it suggests, rename any, then click Apply. Nothing changes until you do.
cards.note: Tidy needs intelligence, which is off until you turn it on.

cards.title: Pin a site to the top of the sidebar
questions: keep a site at the top
steps: Right-click the tab in the sidebar and choose Pin Tab, or drag it to the top.
Pinned tabs show as icons at the top of the Space and keep the address you pinned.
cards.note: A Space holds up to 12 pinned tabs.

cards.title: Unpin a tab
questions: take a site off the top
steps: Right-click the pinned tab and choose Unpin Tab.
It moves down to your open tabs. Close it there if you don't need it.

cards.title: Keep a tab in the sidebar
questions: stop a tab from being archived
steps: Drag the tab above the line in the sidebar.
Or right-click it and choose Save in Folder > Saved Tabs.
Saved tabs stay until you delete them and keep the address you saved.

cards.title: Remove a saved tab
steps: Right-click the saved tab in the sidebar.
Choose Delete Tab to remove it, or Move to Current Tabs to make it an ordinary open tab.

cards.title: Go back to a pinned or saved tab's original page
questions: reset pinned tab to its home page
back to the original page of a pinned tab
steps: Double-click the pinned or saved tab in the sidebar.
Or right-click it and choose Edit Tab > Return to Saved URL.

cards.title: Change the page a pinned or saved tab keeps
questions: set a new home page for a pinned tab
steps: Go to the page you want the tab to keep.
Right-click the tab and choose Edit Tab > Replace with Current URL.

cards.title: Choose where a pinned tab reopens after you close it
questions: pinned tab reopens on the wrong page
click favicon to go back to saved url
aliases: Click the favicon to return to the saved URL
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Tabs.
Under Pinned and saved tabs, set After closing to Resume last location or Return to saved URL.
Turn on Click the favicon to return to the saved URL if you like.

cards.title: Rename a tab
questions: give a tab a custom name
steps: Right-click the tab in the sidebar.
Choose Rename Tab. For a pinned or saved tab, it's under Edit Tab.
Type the new name and press Return.

cards.title: Give pinned and saved tabs short, tidy titles
steps: In Settings > Search > Tab organization, turn on Enable suggestions and pick a Tab organization model. Tidy titles when pinning is then on.
To tidy one tab, right-click it and choose Edit Tab > Tidy Title.
To undo, choose Edit Tab > Restore Original Title.
cards.note: These need intelligence, which is off until you turn it on.

cards.title: Change a tab's icon
questions: use an emoji for a tab
steps: Right-click the tab in the sidebar. For a pinned or saved tab, open Edit Tab.
Choose Change Icon… to pick an emoji or symbol, or Pull New Icon to fetch the site's icon again.

cards.title: Duplicate a tab
steps: Right-click the tab in the sidebar and choose Duplicate Tab.
Or choose Tabs > Duplicate Tab.

cards.title: Mute a tab that's playing sound
questions: stop the noise from a tab
steps: Look for the speaker mark on a tab in the sidebar.
Click it to mute the tab. Click it again to unmute.
cards.note: The player at the bottom of the sidebar also has a Mute button.

cards.title: Keep a tab from going to sleep
questions: don't put this tab to sleep
keep a page running in the background
steps: Right-click the tab in the sidebar.
Choose Keep Loaded. Choose Stop Keeping Loaded to undo it.
cards.note: Ode may still unload it if your Mac runs very low on memory.

cards.title: Put a tab to sleep to free memory
steps: Right-click the tab in the sidebar and choose Unload Tab.
The tab stays in the sidebar and loads again when you click it.
cards.note: Middle-clicking a pinned tab also unloads it.

cards.title: Change when tabs go to sleep
questions: tabs reload when i come back
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Appearance.
Under Sleeping tabs, set Put tabs to sleep after to 5, 15 or 30 minutes, 1 or 3 hours, or Never.
cards.note: The default is 15 minutes. The five tabs you looked at most recently never sleep, and a tab in a Space that no window shows sleeps after half the time.

cards.title: Move to the next or previous tab with the keyboard
steps: Choose Tabs > Next Tab or Previous Tab.
To jump to a tab by its place, press Command and a number from 1 to 9.

cards.title: Jump back to the tab you were just on
steps: Choose Tabs > Most Recent Tab.
Do it again to flip back.
cards.note: It jumps straight to the tab. There's no tab switcher panel.

cards.title: Select several tabs at once
steps: Command-click tabs in the sidebar to pick them, or Shift-click to pick a range.
Right-click one of them to pin, move, split, duplicate, archive or delete them together.

cards.title: Move a tab up or down the sidebar
questions: drag tab to a different place
steps: Drag the tab up or down in the sidebar.
Drop it above the line to save it, or into a folder to file it.

cards.title: Nest tabs opened from a page under it
questions: show which tab a link came from
aliases: Nest tabs opened from a page
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Appearance.
Under Layout, turn on Nest tabs opened from a page.
Links you open in a new tab now appear under the tab they came from.
cards.note: Only open tabs nest. Closing a tab moves the tabs under it up a level instead of closing them, and tabs on top or in the icon sidebar show without nesting.

cards.title: Nest a tab under another, or move it out
questions: nest a tab under another tab
make a tab a child of another
move a tab out of a tree
steps: Right-click an open tab and choose Nest Under Tab Above.
To take it out again, right-click it and choose Move Out a Level.
Or drag a tab onto the middle of another open tab to nest it there.
cards.note: These need Nest tabs opened from a page turned on in Settings > Appearance > Layout. With it off, dropping a tab on another makes a folder.

cards.title: Hide the tabs nested under a tab
questions: what is the number next to my tab
steps: Move the pointer over a tab that has tabs under it and click the arrow beside its close button.
Or right-click the tab and choose Hide Nested Tabs. The number beside it shows how many are hidden.
Click the number, or choose Show Nested Tabs, to see them again.
cards.note: Next Tab and Previous Tab skip hidden tabs. Closing a collapsed tab doesn't close the tabs under it.

cards.title: Make a folder for tabs
questions: make a new folder in the sidebar
how do i add a folder
steps: Click the ••• button beside the Space's name and choose New Folder, then type its name.
Or right-click an open tab and choose Add to Current Tabs Folder > New Folder.
Drag tabs onto the folder to file them.

cards.title: Put a folder inside another folder
steps: Right-click a folder and choose New Nested Folder.
Or drag a folder onto another folder.
cards.note: Folders can nest up to 16 levels deep.

cards.title: Move tabs into a folder
questions: put several tabs in a folder
steps: Drag the tab onto the folder in the sidebar.
Or right-click the tab and choose Save in Folder, or Add to Current Tabs Folder for an open tab.
To move several, select them first, then right-click and choose Move to Folder.

cards.title: Rename a folder
steps: Right-click the folder and choose Rename Folder.
Type the new name and press Return.

cards.title: Change a folder's color or icon
steps: Right-click the folder and choose Folder Color… or Folder Icon.
Pick a color, an emoji or a symbol.
To show only the icon, turn on Icon Only Folders in Settings > Appearance.

cards.title: Move a folder between saved and open tabs
questions: keep a folder of open tabs
steps: Right-click the folder.
Choose Move to Saved Tabs or Move to Current Tabs. Its tabs and nested folders go with it.
Or drag the folder across the line.

cards.title: Delete a folder
questions: get rid of a folder but keep tabs
steps: Right-click the folder and choose Delete Folder.
Confirm. Its tabs stay in the same section, and nested folders move up one level.

cards.title: See two tabs side by side with Split View
questions: view two websites next to each other
steps: Drag a tab from the sidebar onto the page you're looking at.
Or right-click a tab in the sidebar and choose Split with Current Tab.
Click a side to choose which page the keyboard and address bar use.
cards.note: Split With Next Tab splits the current tab with the one below it.

cards.title: Add a third or fourth tab to Split View
questions: add another tab to split view
steps: Drag another tab from the sidebar onto the Split View.
Or right-click the tab and choose Split with Current Tab.
A Split View holds up to four tabs.

cards.title: Open a link beside the current page
questions: open a link side by side
open link next to this page
steps: Right-click a link on the page.
Choose Open Link in Split View.

cards.title: Switch between the sides of a Split View
steps: Click the side you want to use. Its border shows it has focus.
Or use Focus Next Split Card and Focus Previous Split Card from the Tabs menu.

cards.title: Make Split View follow your pointer
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Tabs.
Turn on Focus follows pointer.

cards.title: Make one side of a Split View wider
steps: Drag the line between the two pages left or right.

cards.title: Swap the sides of a Split View
questions: put this page on the other side
steps: Click the page you want to move.
Choose Tabs > Move Split Card Left or Move Split Card Right.

cards.title: Take one tab out of a Split View
questions: take a page out of split
leave split view with one tab
steps: Click the page you want to take out.
Choose Tabs > Remove Tab From Split. The other tabs stay together.

cards.title: End a Split View
steps: Choose Tabs > Separate All Tabs. Every page becomes its own tab again.
To close all its tabs instead, right-click the Split View in the sidebar and choose Close Split.

cards.title: Name a Split View or change its color or icon
steps: Right-click the Split View's row in the sidebar.
Choose Rename Split View…, Change Icon… or Change Color.

cards.title: What a Space is
steps: A Space is a set of tabs with its own sign-ins, history, passwords and extensions.
Use one for work and one for personal browsing, and switch between them in one window.
A site signed in to in one Space isn't signed in to in another.

cards.title: Make a new Space
questions: how do i make a work space
steps: Right-click an empty part of the sidebar and choose New Space.
Give it a name, a color and an icon.
Or choose Ode > Settings and click + beside the Spaces heading.
cards.note: You can have up to 64 Spaces.

cards.title: Switch to another Space
steps: Press Control-1 to Control-9 to jump to a Space by its place, as in Arc.
Or click the Space's icon at the bottom of the sidebar.
Or swipe left or right with two fingers over the sidebar.
cards.note: Option-Command-Right Arrow and Option-Command-Left Arrow move to the next or previous Space. Control-Right Arrow and Control-Left Arrow do too, once macOS stops using them for Mission Control.

cards.title: Switch Spaces with the keyboard
questions: control left and right for spaces
steps: Press Control-1 to Control-9 to go to a Space by its place in the sidebar, as in Arc.
Press Option-Command-Right Arrow or Option-Command-Left Arrow for the next or previous Space.
cards.note: Control-Right Arrow and Control-Left Arrow switch Spaces too, once you turn off Move left a space and Move right a space in System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > Mission Control.

cards.title: Change a Space's name, color or icon
questions: change the color of the sidebar
steps: Right-click an empty part of the sidebar and choose Edit Space.
On the Appearance page, type a name, click a color and pick an icon: a symbol, an emoji or a letter.

cards.title: Change the order of your Spaces
steps: Choose Ode > Settings.
Click the pencil beside the Spaces heading, drag the Spaces into order, then click the checkmark.
Or right-click a Space there and choose Move Up or Move Down.
cards.note: The order sets which Space Control-1 to Control-9 open.

cards.title: Delete a Space
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click the Space in the sidebar, then click Browsing.
Click the Delete button with the Space's name at the bottom, then confirm with Delete Space and Data.
cards.note: This removes the Space's tabs, history, passwords, sign-ins and extensions. Downloaded files stay. You can't delete your last Space.

cards.title: Move a tab to another Space
steps: Right-click the tab and choose Move to Space, then pick the Space.
Or drag the tab onto the Space's icon at the bottom of the sidebar.
cards.note: The tab opens with the other Space's sign-ins, not the ones it had.

cards.title: Stay put or follow a tab when you move it to another Space
questions: stop switching space when moving tab
stay in this space after moving a tab
aliases: Follow tabs moved to another Space
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Tabs.
Turn Follow tabs moved to another Space on or off.

cards.title: Use two accounts on the same site
steps: Make a Space for each account.
Sign in to the site once in each Space. Each Space keeps its own sign-ins.
Switch Spaces to switch accounts.

cards.title: Give a Space its own search engine
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click the Space, then click Browsing.
Pick an engine under Search with.

cards.title: Choose the Space Ode opens in
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click General.
Under Startup, choose the Default Space and what happens When Ode opens.

cards.title: Lock a Space with Touch ID
questions: put a password on a space
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click the Space, then click Privacy.
Under Lock, turn on Require Touch ID or password.
The Space locks again whenever Ode goes to the background.
cards.note: A locked Space keeps its tabs and history. It only asks who you are before it shows them.

cards.title: Hide or show the sidebar
steps: Choose View > Toggle Sidebar. The sidebar slides away and the page fills the window.
While it's hidden, move the pointer to the window's edge. The sidebar comes out over the page until you move away.
To keep it shown again, choose Toggle Sidebar or click the sidebar button at the bottom of the sidebar.
cards.note: With tabs on top, Command-S hides the bar of tabs, and the top edge brings it back.

cards.title: Stop the hidden sidebar from coming out at the window's edge
questions: stop the sidebar appearing at the edge
hidden sidebar shows when i move the mouse to the side
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Appearance.
Under Window, turn off Show sidebar at window edge.
cards.note: It's on by default. With it off, click the window's edge or press Command-S to bring the sidebar back.

cards.title: Change how easily a hidden sidebar slides out
questions: hidden sidebar comes out too easily
how close to the edge does the pointer need to be
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Appearance.
Under Window, drag the Sidebar hover area slider. Smaller means you have to reach closer to the edge.
cards.note: The slider works while Show sidebar at window edge is on.

cards.title: Put the sidebar on the right
questions: put the sidebar back on the left
steps: Choose View > Move Sidebar to the Right.
To move it back, choose View > Move Sidebar to the Left.
cards.note: It's also Sidebar on right in Settings > Appearance > Layout. It isn't available while tabs are on top.

cards.title: Make the sidebar wider or narrower
steps: Move the pointer to the sidebar's edge beside the page.
Drag it left or right.
cards.note: Double-click the edge to go back to the standard width. Dragging it far in shows the sidebar as icons, then hides it.

cards.title: Show the sidebar as icons
steps: Choose View > Show Sidebar as Icons, or drag the sidebar's edge in until it turns into icons.
Rest the pointer on an icon to see its title.
To see titles again, choose View > Show Full Sidebar or drag the edge out.
cards.note: It's also Sidebar in Settings > Appearance > Layout. Dragging the edge narrower than 150 points switches to icons, and narrower than 60 points hides the sidebar. Icons aren't available with tabs on top.

cards.title: Show tabs across the top of the window
questions: put tabs back in the sidebar
steps: Choose View > Show Tabs on Top.
The bar holds the Space's menu, pinned tabs as icons, then saved and open tabs.
To go back, choose View > Show Tabs in Sidebar.
cards.note: It's also Tabs in Settings > Appearance > Layout. Folders, History and Downloads open the sidebar over the page.

cards.title: Use light or dark mode
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Appearance.
Under Window, set Appearance to System, Light or Dark.
cards.note: To darken a website itself, use a Boost.

cards.title: Choose the color of selected tabs and the address bar
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Appearance.
Turn off Follow Space accent to pick your own color. Leave it on to use each Space's color.

cards.title: Make tabs bigger, smaller or rounder
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Appearance.
Under Tabs and pins, set Tab scale to Small, Default or Large, and change the corner radius and pin layout. The preview shows the result.
cards.note: Reset All… at the bottom puts every appearance choice back.

cards.title: Fit more tabs with Compact density
questions: fit more tabs in the sidebar
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Appearance.
Under Layout, set Density to Compact. Rows, pinned tabs and the address field get shorter.
cards.note: Comfortable is the default. To make text and icons smaller too, change Tab scale.

cards.title: Control music and video from the sidebar
questions: player at the bottom of the sidebar
steps: Play sound or video in a tab, then switch to another tab. The player appears at the bottom of the sidebar.
Use its buttons to play, pause, skip or mute.
To turn the player off, go to Settings > Tabs > Sidebar widgets and turn off Now Playing.
cards.note: The keyboard's play-pause key controls it too. The player hides while its tab is on screen.

cards.title: Go back to the tab that's playing
questions: go back to the tab playing music
find the tab that's playing in another space
return to the tab with the music
steps: Click the player's artwork or title at the bottom of the sidebar, or its Back to Tab button.
Or choose Tabs > Back to Playing Tab from any window.
cards.note: Ode finds the tab in whatever Space or window it's in. A locked Space asks you to unlock it first.

cards.title: Where History, Archive and Downloads are
questions: where are downloads in the sidebar
steps: Click the list button at the bottom of the sidebar, beside the Space icons.
Choose Archive, History or Downloads. Each shows only the current Space.

cards.title: Use Ode in full screen
steps: Choose View > Enter Full Screen.
Choose View > Exit Full Screen to leave.

cards.title: Open a new window
steps: Choose File > New Window.
Both windows show the same Spaces and tabs. Each keeps its own selected Space and tab.

cards.title: Open a temporary window that keeps nothing
steps: Choose File > New Blank Window.
It uses the current Space's sign-ins and passwords, but its tabs and history go away when you close it.
cards.note: For browsing without your sign-ins, use a private window.

cards.title: Browse privately
steps: Choose File > New Private Window.
Ode keeps no history from it, uses no saved passwords, and forgets sign-ins when you close it.
Close the window to end private browsing.
cards.note: Private windows search with DuckDuckGo unless you change it in Settings > Search. Websites and your network can still see what you do.

cards.title: Close a window
questions: close all tabs in this window
steps: Choose File > Close Window.
Your tabs stay in the sidebar of your other windows and the next time you open Ode.

cards.title: What happens when you drag a tab out of the window
questions: tab opened in its own window
steps: Dragging a tab outside the window moves it into a temporary window of its own.
Drag it back into a normal window to keep it. Its page closes with the temporary window.

cards.title: Preview a link without leaving the page
questions: open link in a popup preview
look at a link without opening a tab
steps: Option-click a link, or right-click it and choose Open Link in Peek.
Read it in the Peek over your page.
Press Escape to close it, or click Open In… to keep it as a tab.
cards.note: Peek shows only for the tab you opened it from.

cards.title: Choose when links open in Peek
questions: links from pinned tabs open in a preview
aliases: Open cross-site links from pinned and saved tabs in Peek
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Links.
Under Peek, turn Open cross-site links from pinned and saved tabs in Peek on or off.
Set Open Peek with to Option or Command. The other key opens a new tab.

cards.title: Drag a link to preview it
steps: Drag a link a little way off the page. A live preview follows the pointer.
Let go to keep it open in Peek.
Hold Option while you drag to move the link itself instead.
cards.note: Turn this off with Drag links to Peek in Settings > Links.

cards.title: Open a small Quick Window
questions: small window for links from other apps
steps: Choose File > New Quick Window, then type an address or search.
To keep the page, click Open in and pick a Space.
Close the Quick Window to drop it. It waits in Archive for a while.
cards.note: Option-Command-N opens it, as it opened Little Arc.

cards.title: Choose where links from other apps open
questions: links from slack open in a quick window
where do links from other apps open
open external links in my main space
links from email open in wrong space
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Links.
Under Links from other apps, set Open in to Quick Window, Most Recent Space or Chosen Space.
cards.note: Link routing rules run first.

cards.title: Choose how long Quick Windows are kept
questions: where did my quick window go
find a quick window i closed
aliases: Remember the chosen Space for each site
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Links.
Under Quick Window, set Auto-archive to 1, 6, 12 or 24 hours, or Never.
Closed Quick Windows are in Archive under Quick Windows.

cards.title: Send links from other apps to the right Space
questions: open github links in my work space
zoom links open in personal profile
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click Links, then click New Route under Routing.
Choose Contains or Is Exactly and type part of the address, such as github.com.
Pick the Space under Open in Space. The first matching route wins.
cards.note: Routes apply to links you click in other apps, not links inside Ode.

cards.title: Open a link in another Space
questions: open this link in my work space
steps: Right-click the link on the page.
Choose Open Link in Another Space, then pick the Space.

cards.title: Make Ode your default browser
questions: open links in ode instead of safari
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click General.
Beside Default browser, click Make Default.
Confirm in the question macOS shows.

cards.title: Why a small window opened when I signed in
questions: sign in with google opened a small window
why did a popup window open
steps: When a site opens a pop-up, such as Sign in with Google, Ode shows it in a Quick Window in the same Space.
It closes by itself when you finish signing in.

cards.title: Find a word on the page
questions: look for a word on this page
steps: Choose Page > Find in Page and type what you're looking for.
Use the arrows to go to the next or previous match.
Click Close Find or press Escape when you're done.
cards.note: Chromium pages show how many matches there are. WebKit pages show only whether there's a match.

cards.title: Make a page bigger or smaller
steps: Choose Page > Zoom In or Zoom Out.
Choose Page > Actual Size to go back to normal.

cards.title: Set a zoom level for every page
questions: set page zoom for all sites
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Appearance.
Under Page, pick a Default page zoom from 50% to 300%.

cards.title: Read an article without clutter
steps: Open the article.
Choose Page > Show Reader. Choose Hide Reader to go back.
cards.note: Reader works on WebKit pages. On a Chromium page, choose Page > Open Page in WebKit first.

cards.title: Translate a page
steps: Choose Page > Translate Page.
To pick the languages, choose View > Show Translation Toolbar.
Choose Show Original in the toolbar to undo it.
cards.note: Translation runs on your Mac with Apple's languages. Macs may need to download a language first.

cards.title: Translate pages automatically
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click General.
Under Translation, turn on Translate automatically and choose the languages.
Turn off Offer to translate pages if you don't want to be asked.

cards.title: Copy the link to the current page
steps: Choose Page > Copy Page Link.
Paste it anywhere.

cards.title: Copy a page link as Markdown
steps: Choose Page > Copy Page Link as Markdown.
Paste it into notes or a document. It has the page's title and address.

cards.title: Share a page
steps: Choose Page > Share.
Pick how to share it, such as AirDrop, Messages or Mail.

cards.title: Print a page
steps: Choose File > Print.
Pick your printer and click Print.

cards.title: Save a page as a PDF
steps: Choose Page > Export as PDF.
Choose where to save it and click Save.

cards.title: Save a whole page to read offline
steps: Choose Page > Save Web Archive.
Choose where to save it. Open it later with File > Open File.
cards.note: WebKit pages save a .webarchive file and Chromium pages an .mhtml file. Each engine opens only its own kind.

cards.title: Open a file from your Mac
steps: Choose File > Open File.
Pick the file. It opens as a tab in the current Space.

cards.title: Reload a page
steps: Choose Navigate > Reload Page.
If it still looks wrong, choose Navigate > Reload from Origin to skip saved copies.
Choose Navigate > Stop Loading to stop.

cards.title: Go back or forward a page
steps: Click the back or forward arrow at the top of the sidebar.
Or swipe left or right with two fingers on the page.
cards.note: Right-click the back arrow to see earlier pages.

cards.title: Keep a video playing in a small floating window
questions: keep video playing when switching tabs
why doesn't my video float when i switch tabs
turn off automatic picture in picture
aliases: Picture in Picture when switching tabs
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click General, and turn on Picture in Picture when switching tabs.
Play a video and switch to another tab. The video keeps playing in a small window.
cards.note: It's on by default. A video that plays muted by itself stays on its page unless you started it, and some sites don't allow it.

cards.title: Take a screenshot of part of a page
questions: take a screenshot of a website
copy part of the page as image
steps: Click Site Controls at the right of the address, then click Capture.
Drag a rectangle over the part you want. It's copied, ready to paste.
For the whole page, use Copy Full Page Capture in the developer toolbar.

cards.title: What's in Site Controls
questions: the button next to the address
steps: Click Site Controls, the slider button at the right of the address.
It has quick buttons, Boost, the page's engine, content blocking, security and the site's permissions.

cards.title: Search the web for selected text
questions: search with google from right click
steps: Select the text on the page.
Right-click it and choose Search with and your search engine's name.

cards.title: Preview a site at phone or desktop size
steps: Choose Develop > Show Developer Toolbar.
Open Viewport Preview and choose a phone or desktop size, or Custom.
Choose Normal — Preview Off to go back.
cards.note: The toolbar opens by itself on local pages such as localhost. Turn that off in Settings > General.

cards.title: Inspect a page's code
steps: Choose Develop > Show Web Inspector.
It opens inside the window for the page you're on. Do the same to close it.
cards.note: Chromium pages open Chromium DevTools. WebKit pages open Web Inspector.

cards.title: Restyle a website with a Boost
questions: how do i make a boost
steps: Open the site and choose Page > Boost This Site.
Use the Boost bar over the page: Colors, Font, Zap to hide things, or CSS.
Click Done. Ode saves it and applies it every time you visit the site in this Space.
cards.note: Boosts work on Chromium and WebKit pages, one per site in each Space.

cards.title: Find and edit a Boost you made
steps: Go to the site the Boost is for.
Click Site Controls at the right of the address, then click Edit beside Boost.
Or choose Page > Boost This Site.
cards.note: There is no list of every Boost yet. Each one lives with its site.

cards.title: Make a website dark or change its colors
steps: Choose Page > Boost This Site, then click Colors.
Turn on Dark, pick a Tint, or move the Brightness and Contrast sliders.
Click Reset Colors to start over, then Done.

cards.title: Change a website's font
questions: use a different font for this site
steps: Choose Page > Boost This Site.
Open Font and pick one, such as New York, Georgia or Rounded.
Choose Site's Font to go back to the original.

cards.title: Hide parts of a website
questions: hide an element on a page
steps: Choose Page > Boost This Site, then click Zap.
Click each thing on the page you want to hide. Press Escape to stop.
Click Done. Those parts stay hidden on that site.

cards.title: Bring back something you hid with Zap
steps: Choose Page > Boost This Site.
Click the Hidden button in the Boost bar.
Choose one item to show it again, or Show All.

cards.title: Add your own CSS to a website
steps: Choose Page > Boost This Site, then click CSS.
Type your CSS and click Apply.

cards.title: Turn a Boost off for a while
steps: Go to the site and click Site Controls at the right of the address.
Turn off the switch beside Boost. Turn it on again whenever you like.

cards.title: Delete a Boost
steps: Choose Page > Boost This Site.
Click the ••• button in the Boost bar and choose Remove Boost.

cards.title: Where Boosts apply and whether they sync
questions: why doesn't my boost work in another space
steps: A Boost belongs to one site in one Space. Make it again in another Space to use it there.
Boosts stay on this Mac. They're saved in Ode's export but don't sync.
cards.note: A Space keeps up to 500 Boosts.

cards.title: See new mail and your next meeting from a pinned tab
questions: hover pinned tab to see email
steps: Pin or save Gmail or Google Calendar and open it once.
Its icon shows your unread count, or how soon your next meeting starts.
Rest the pointer on the tab to see recent mail or upcoming events.
cards.note: Previews read from the tab's own page and stay on this Mac.

cards.title: Turn tab previews off
aliases: Show previews of pinned and saved tabs
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Tabs.
Under Tab previews, turn off Show previews of pinned and saved tabs, or just Gmail or Google Calendar.
You can also turn off Tab Previews in Site Controls on those sites.

cards.title: Why a tab preview is empty or out of date
steps: Previews read from the tab itself, so open the pinned tab once after Ode starts.
A sleeping tab keeps its last preview. Choose Keep Loaded on the tab to keep it fresh.
If it says you're signed out, sign in to the site in that tab.
cards.note: Previews work for Gmail and Google Calendar, in pinned and saved tabs.

cards.title: See your downloads
steps: Choose View > Show Downloads.
Or click the list button at the bottom of the sidebar and choose Downloads.
Each Space shows only its own downloads.

cards.title: The downloads at the bottom of the sidebar
questions: get rid of finished downloads in sidebar
steps: Running and just-finished downloads show above the Space icons, up to three at a time.
Click Hide to put away the finished ones, or Downloads to see them all.
A finished file stays there for an hour.

cards.title: Drag a download into another app
questions: drag file from downloads to finder
steps: Show your downloads, or find the file at the bottom of the sidebar.
Drag the finished file into Finder, Mail, Messages or a page's upload box.

cards.title: Open, preview or delete a downloaded file
steps: Right-click a finished download in the list.
Choose Open, Show in Finder, Quick Look or Copy.
Choose Move to Trash to delete the file, or Remove from List to keep the file and hide the row.
cards.note: Rest the pointer on a finished download and press the Space bar to preview it.

cards.title: Pause, resume or cancel a download
steps: Right-click the download that's running.
Choose Pause Download, Resume Download or Cancel Download.
cards.note: Pause and resume depend on the page's engine and the site.

cards.title: Clear the downloads list
steps: Show your downloads and click Filter Downloads.
Choose Clear Downloads. The files stay on your Mac.

cards.title: Choose where downloads are saved
aliases: Ask where to save each download
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click the Space, then click Browsing.
Under Downloads, click Choose Folder…, or turn on Ask where to save each download.
cards.note: Each Space has its own download folder.

cards.title: Why a download was blocked
questions: site wants to download multiple files
steps: Ode blocks a site from downloading several files on its own, and warns about files that came over an insecure connection.
If you trust it, right-click the download and choose Allow Download.
To let a site download without asking, change Automatic Downloads in its Site Controls.

cards.title: What the downloads list keeps after you quit
questions: where did my download history go
steps: Each Space keeps its finished, canceled and failed downloads when you quit and open Ode again.
A download older than the Space's Download Records setting in Settings > Privacy leaves the list. Clear Downloads empties it at once.
Downloads in a private window are never kept. Your files stay in your download folder either way. The list stays on this Mac: it isn't synced or exported.

cards.title: See your browsing history
questions: see sites i went to yesterday
steps: Choose View > Show History.
Type to search, or open the filter menu to show Today, Past Week or Past Month.
Click a page to open it again.
cards.note: Each Space has its own history.

cards.title: Find a page you visited before
questions: find a page i visited last week
steps: Open the Command Bar and type part of the page's title or address.
Type @history and a space first to see only history.
Or choose View > Show History and use its search field.
cards.note: History search matches titles and addresses, not the words on the page.

cards.title: Remove one page from your history
steps: Open the Command Bar and type until the page shows.
Move down to it with the arrow keys and press Shift-Delete.

cards.title: Clear your history
steps: Choose View > Show History.
Open the filter menu and choose Clear History, then confirm.
cards.note: This clears the current Space only. Other Spaces keep their history.

cards.title: Choose how long history and Archive are kept
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click the Space, then click Privacy.
Under Keep, choose how long to keep History, Archived Tabs and Download Records: from 1 Day to Forever.
cards.note: Shortening it deletes older records at once, so Ode asks first.

cards.title: Find tabs that were closed or archived
steps: Choose View > Show Archive, or click the list button at the bottom of the sidebar and choose Archive.
Search or filter by Closed, Automatically Cleaned or Quick Windows.
Click a tab to bring it back.
cards.note: To find archived tabs from the Command Bar too, turn on Archived Tabs under Sections in Settings > Search.

cards.title: Get your tabs back from an earlier copy
steps: Choose File > Restore from an Earlier Copy.
Pick a copy by its date, Spaces and tab count, then click Restore and reopen.
Ode quits and opens again with that copy. Your current tabs are kept as a copy too.
cards.note: Ode keeps a copy each time it starts and before each update.

cards.title: What “Some tabs are missing” means
steps: Ode shows this when many Spaces or tabs vanished without you closing them.
Click Restore that copy to go back to the earlier copy, or Keep this session if you closed them yourself.

cards.title: Ode won't open or keeps crashing at startup
steps: Hold Shift while you open Ode, then choose Start in safe mode. Ode offers this by itself after two failed starts.
Safe mode pauses sync and loads pages only when you open them. Nothing is deleted.
If that fails too, choose Restore from an earlier copy.

cards.title: Find a crash report to share
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click About.
Under Crash and hang reports, click View on a report.
Use Copy report or Save report… to share it.
cards.note: Reports stay on your Mac for 30 days and never include the pages you visit. Ode can't send them for you yet.

cards.title: Ode backs up your tabs every day
questions: does ode back up my tabs
steps: Ode writes your Spaces, tabs, bookmarks and history to Documents > Ode Export every day, and soon after you change your pinned tabs or folders.
It keeps the last 7 exports. Passwords and cookies are never written.
Change it in Settings > Advanced > Automatic export.
cards.note: Exports wait while any Space is locked.

cards.title: Export your tabs and bookmarks
questions: take my data to another browser
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Advanced.
Click Export Now for a full export, or Export Bookmarks as HTML… for a file other browsers can import.
cards.note: Exports never include passwords, cookies, website data or extensions.

cards.title: Bring back Spaces from an Ode export
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Advanced.
Click Import Browser Data… and choose the Ode Browser Data.json file.
Its Spaces are added after yours.

cards.title: Move everything over from Arc
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click Advanced, then click Import from Another Browser… and pick Arc. New users see this during setup.
Review each Space. Click anything to leave it out, and choose where it goes.
Click Import. Ode brings your Spaces, tabs, folders, archive, history, passwords and sign-ins.
cards.note: macOS asks once to let Ode read Arc's saved passwords.

cards.title: Where my Arc favorites, pinned tabs and Today tabs went
questions: where did my arc favorites go
where are my arc pinned tabs
steps: Arc's favorites became pinned tabs at the top. Past 12, the rest went into a saved folder called Imported Pinned Tabs.
Arc's pinned tabs became saved tabs, in the same folders.
Today tabs became open tabs, and Arc's archive is in Archive.

cards.title: Import from Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Zen or another browser
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click Advanced, then click Import from Another Browser.
Pick the browser. If it isn't listed, click Scan for more.
Review what comes over, then click Import.
cards.note: Passwords come from Chromium browsers such as Chrome, Brave and Edge. Safari, Firefox and Zen passwords stay there.

cards.title: Why I'm signed out of sites after importing
questions: do i have to log in again
steps: Sign-ins come over only from Arc, and only on pages that open in Chromium.
From other browsers, sign in to each site once in the right Space.
Ode Passwords can fill your imported passwords as you sign in.

cards.title: Bring your extensions from Arc or Chrome
steps: The import review lists each Space's Chrome Web Store extensions. Turn off any you don't want.
After the import, Ode offers to install the rest in their Spaces.

cards.title: See your saved passwords
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click the Space, then click Passwords.
Click an account to see it. Ode asks for Touch ID or your Mac password before showing or copying a password.
cards.note: Each Space has its own passwords.

cards.title: Stop Ode from offering to save passwords
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click the Space, then click Passwords.
Turn off Use Ode Passwords. Saved passwords stay until you delete them.

cards.title: Make a strong password for a new account
steps: Click into the password field of a sign-up form. Ode offers a strong password.
Click Use Strong Password. Ode saves it in the Space first, then fills it in.

cards.title: Import passwords from a file
steps: Export your passwords as a CSV file from the other app.
Choose Ode > Settings, click the Space, click Passwords, then click Import Passwords.
Choose the file, review the accounts and import. Then delete the CSV file.
cards.note: Ode reads Chrome-style, Safari, Firefox and Bitwarden CSV files.

cards.title: Export your passwords
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click the Space, then click Passwords.
Click Export Passwords… and confirm with Touch ID or your Mac password.
Anyone with the file can read it, so delete it once you've used it.

cards.title: Keep Ode passwords in iCloud Keychain
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click the Space, then click Passwords.
Turn on Sync with iCloud Keychain.
Turn on Offer a copy to Passwords to also let Apple's Passwords app save new passwords.

cards.title: Use 1Password, Bitwarden or another password manager
steps: Install its extension from the Chrome Web Store in each Space you use it in.
For 1Password, also allow Ode in the 1Password app when it asks.
cards.note: Extensions run only on pages that open in Chromium.

cards.title: Sign in with passkeys
questions: use touch id to sign in to website
steps: Ode for Mac can't use the passkeys saved on your Mac yet. It's waiting for Apple's approval.
Sign in with a password for now. Check the status in Settings > Privacy & Permissions > Passkeys.

cards.title: Fill in addresses and credit cards
steps: Ode doesn't fill in addresses or payment cards, and doesn't offer Apple Pay on websites yet.
A password manager extension that fills cards works on Chromium pages.

cards.title: How Ode blocks ads and trackers
steps: Blocking is on in every Space from the start.
Chromium and WebKit pages both use Ode's own blocker, with the filter lists ad blockers use: EasyList, EasyPrivacy and uBlock Origin's lists, plus one for your language.
On WebKit pages, Site Controls shows what a page blocked.

cards.title: Turn off ad blocking for one site
questions: page not working turn off blocker
aliases: Block ads and trackers on this site
steps: Click Site Controls at the right of the address.
Turn off Block ads and trackers on this site. The page reloads.

cards.title: Turn ad blocking on or off
questions: disable ad blocker in a space
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Ad Blocking.
Choose Off to stop blocking in every Space, or Balanced or Strict to turn it back on.

cards.title: Let a site use your camera, microphone or location
steps: Click Site Controls at the right of the address.
Under Permissions, set Camera, Microphone or Location to Allow.
If it still doesn't work, check that macOS allows Ode in Settings > Privacy & Permissions.

cards.title: Check that macOS lets Ode use the camera or microphone
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Privacy & Permissions.
Under System permissions, check Camera, Microphone, Location, Notifications and Files & Folders, and fix any that need it.

cards.title: Reset what you allowed or blocked for sites
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click the Space, then click Privacy.
Under Site permissions, choose Ask Again for one site, or click Reset All… for every site.
cards.note: Each Space keeps its own permissions.

cards.title: Allow pop-ups for a site
steps: When a pop-up is blocked, a dot appears on Site Controls. Click it.
Click Allow Automatic Pop-ups, then try the button on the page again.

cards.title: Get or stop notifications from a site
steps: Click Site Controls and set Notifications to Allow or Block.
Make sure macOS allows Ode's notifications in Settings > Privacy & Permissions.
cards.note: Sites can notify you only while Ode is open.

cards.title: Is this site's connection secure
steps: Look at the lock at the left of the address. It says whether the connection is secure.
Click it, or look under Security in Site Controls, to review the certificate.
cards.note: Don't type passwords or card numbers on a page marked Not Secure.

cards.title: A website isn't working properly
questions: can't log in to a site
steps: Reload the page. If an ad blocker might be the cause, turn off Block ads and trackers on this site in Site Controls.
Try the other engine: choose Page > Open Page in WebKit or Open Page in Chromium.
Check you're in the right Space, since each Space has its own sign-ins.

cards.title: What Ode sends and keeps
steps: Ode needs no account. Your tabs, history and passwords are kept on your Mac.
Search suggestions send what you type to your search engine. Turn them off in Settings > Search.
Intelligence and automatic update checks stay off until you turn them on.

cards.title: Install a Chrome extension
steps: Switch to the Space that should have the extension.
Open the extension's page in the Chrome Web Store and click its Add to Chrome button.
Check the review, then click Add Extension.
cards.note: Extensions run only on pages that open in Chromium.

cards.title: Use an extension in more than one Space
aliases: Install a copy in other spaces
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click the Space that has the extension, then click Extensions.
Expand the extension and click Install a copy in other spaces.
Pick the Spaces. Each copy has its own settings and data.

cards.title: Pin an extension so it's always in view
steps: Click Site Controls at the right of the address. Extensions are listed there.
Right-click the extension and choose Pin to Toolbar. It shows under the address.

cards.title: Turn off or remove an extension
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click the Space, then click Extensions.
Turn the extension's switch off to pause it, or expand it and click Remove Extension.
cards.note: Removing it from one Space leaves it in the others.

cards.title: Set a keyboard shortcut for an extension
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click the Space, then click Extensions.
Click Shortcuts… and set the keys for the extension's commands.
cards.note: Ode's own shortcuts win when both use the same keys.

cards.title: An extension isn't working
questions: why doesn't my extension work on this page
steps: Check the page runs in Chromium. Extensions don't run on WebKit pages, so choose Page > Open Page in Chromium.
Check you're in the Space where you installed it.
In Settings, turn the extension off and on, or check its site access.

cards.title: Use Firefox add-ons or Safari extensions
steps: Ode can't install Firefox add-ons or Safari extensions.
Most have a Chrome Web Store version. Install that instead.

cards.title: Why Ode has two engines, Chromium and WebKit
steps: Chromium is the engine behind Chrome. It runs Chrome extensions and is the default.
WebKit is the engine behind Safari. It offers Reader and protected video where a site supports Safari.
Your tabs, Spaces and passwords are the same in both, but each keeps its own sign-ins.

cards.title: Choose the engine new pages open in
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Engines.
Under Default engine, choose Chromium or WebKit. Pages already open keep their engine.

cards.title: Open a page in the other engine
questions: try the page in safari engine
steps: Choose Page > Open Page in WebKit, or Open Page in Chromium.
The page reloads in that engine. Other pages keep theirs.

cards.title: Always open a site in one engine
questions: always open this site in webkit
steps: Click Site Controls and change Opens in to the engine you want.
To see or remove these rules, choose Ode > Settings and click Engines.
cards.note: A rule for a site doesn't cover its subdomains.

cards.title: Watch Netflix and other protected video
questions: why did the page switch to webkit
steps: Ode’s Chromium does not include Widevine. Supported protected video uses WebKit.
Choose Page > Open Page in WebKit to try the current page there.
Use Site Controls to keep opening that site in WebKit.
cards.note: Playback still depends on the site supporting Safari.

cards.title: What the small mark on a tab's icon means
questions: what is the mark on my tab
steps: The mark shows the tab runs in the engine that isn't your default.
A blue globe means Chromium. Stacked tiles mean WebKit.

cards.title: Let a coding agent use Ode
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, click Agents and turn on Allow agents to use Ode.
Under Spaces, turn on each Space agents may use.
Under Connect an Agent, click Connect beside your agent, or Copy Setup and paste it into the agent.
cards.note: Agents run on your own plan. Ode runs no model and sends nothing to an AI service.

cards.title: What agents can and can't reach
questions: is it safe to let agents use ode
aliases: Let agents run scripts in pages
steps: Agents reach only the Spaces you turn on, and never a private window or a locked Space's tabs.
They can't read saved passwords, read or type into password, one-time code or card fields, or save a download without you.
Ode asks you before an agent opens a site you haven't allowed for it.

cards.title: Stop an agent working in a tab
steps: Click Stop in the bar above the tab the agent is using.
To end its connection, choose Ode > Settings, click Agents, then Disconnect. Forget makes Ode ask again next time.

cards.title: See what agents did
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Agents.
Look under Activity, newest first. Click Clear to empty it.

cards.title: Why Ode asks before an agent's download
questions: agent wants to download a file
steps: A download that starts in a tab an agent is using waits for you.
Ode names the agent in its question. Allow it, or decline to cancel it.

cards.title: Does Ode use AI
questions: is there ai in this browser
steps: Tab organization is off until you turn on Enable suggestions in Settings > Search > Tab organization.
When it's on, it only tidies tab titles and suggests folders for open tabs. It can run on your Mac only, with nothing sent to an AI service.
Private answers in Command-T use Apple’s on-device model and are enabled separately in Settings > Search > Ode.

cards.title: Turn on intelligence and choose a model
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Search.
Under Tab organization, turn on Enable suggestions.
Pick a Tab organization model: Apple on-device model, Model on this Mac, or ChatGPT with your own plan.
cards.note: With ChatGPT, the tab titles a feature works on are sent to OpenAI.

cards.title: Open Settings
steps: Choose Ode > Settings.
Use Search settings at the top of its sidebar to find a setting by name.
cards.note: You can also type a setting's name in the Command Bar.

cards.title: See all keyboard shortcuts
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Shortcuts.
Search for a command to see its keys. Menu items show their keys too.

cards.title: Change a keyboard shortcut
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Shortcuts.
Click a command's shortcut and press the new keys. Ode warns you if they're already in use.
Use Reset to Default for one, or Reset All… for every shortcut.

cards.title: Update Ode
steps: Ode downloads updates on its own. When one is ready, the sidebar shows Restart to update.
Click Restart to update, or keep working and the update installs when you quit Ode.
cards.note: Automatic updates are on unless you turn them off in Settings > About. To check right away, choose Ode > Check for Updates.

cards.title: Go back to an earlier version
questions: go back to an earlier version
aliases: Go back to an earlier version
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click About.
Click Go back to an earlier version…, choose a version, click Download, then click Go back.
cards.note: Ode checks that the earlier version is signed and notarized like yours, then reopens in it. Your Spaces, tabs and settings stay as they are, and Ode tells you first if the earlier version can't open something this one saved.

cards.title: Get new features sooner with Nightly builds
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click About.
Set Update channel to Stable, Nightly or Development. Stable is best for everyday use.
cards.waitsFor: Nightly and Development update feeds published beside the stable appcast. Add the section back to the install guide when they are.

cards.title: See what's new in Ode
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click About.
Open What's New in Ode to read the latest changes.

cards.title: Report a problem
steps: Write your report and review the screenshot.
Choose Send to Ode, or Copy Text to use another app.
cards.note: Only the report, attached screenshot, and selected app details go to Ode. A failed send keeps your draft.

cards.title: Learn everyday moves with Getting Started
steps: Choose Help > Getting Started with Ode.
Try the seven everyday moves: the Command Bar, searching a site, Split View, Peek, switching Spaces, Boosts and asking an assistant.
Then practice tabs, folders and Split View in an example Space. Your own tabs don't change.
cards.note: Show Me starts a move for you where it can. Ode checks off each move when you make it anywhere, and remembers where you stopped.

cards.title: Run setup again
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Advanced.
Click Review & Customize Setup… to change your Spaces, or Rerun onboarding to start from the welcome screen.

cards.title: Install Ode
questions: does ode run on my mac
steps: Download Ode for Mac from odebrowser.com.
Open the disk image and drag Ode into Applications, then open it from there.
cards.note: Ode needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 26.1 or later.

cards.title: Why Ode asks before quitting
aliases: Quit and cancel the download in progress?
steps: Ode asks when a download is still running, because quitting cancels it.
Click Keep Browsing to let it finish, or Quit to cancel it.

cards.title: Arc's names for things in Ode
questions: i used arc where do i find things
steps: Favorites are pinned tabs, Arc's pinned tabs are saved tabs, and Today tabs are open tabs.
Little Arc is Quick Window, and Air Traffic Control is link routing.
The Library's Archive, History and Downloads are behind the list button at the bottom of the sidebar.

cards.title: Easels
steps: Ode doesn't have Easels yet, and Arc's Easels don't come over in the import.
To clip part of a page, use Capture in Site Controls and paste it where you keep notes.

cards.title: Notes
questions: take a note in the browser
steps: Ode doesn't have notes yet, and Arc's notes don't come over in the import.
Copy Page Link as Markdown is handy for saving a page to the notes app you use.

cards.title: Live Folders
steps: Ode doesn't have Live Folders.
Pinned Gmail and Google Calendar tabs can show what's new when you hover over them.

cards.title: Arc Max, Ask on Page and AI previews
steps: Ode can't summarize or chat about a page, and doesn't rename downloads.
With intelligence on, it can tidy tab titles and suggest folders for open tabs.
To ask an AI something, type chatgpt or claude in the Command Bar and press Tab.

cards.title: Bring over Boosts from Arc
questions: where did my arc boosts go
steps: Arc's Boosts don't come over in the import.
Make them again with Page > Boost This Site. Colors, fonts, Zap and CSS work much as they did in Arc.

cards.title: The same pinned tabs in every Space
steps: Each Space has its own pinned tabs, because each Space has its own sign-ins.
Pin the site in each Space where you want it.

cards.title: Sync tabs between Macs
steps: Sync isn't available in Ode yet. It's waiting for Apple to approve Ode's iCloud access.
To move your setup to another Mac, use Export Now and Import Browser Data… in Settings > Advanced.

cards.title: Ode on iPhone and iPad
steps: Ode for iPhone and iPad isn't available yet. Ode runs on Mac only.

cards.title: Ode on Intel Macs, older macOS, Windows or Linux
questions: does ode work on intel mac
steps: Ode needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 26.1 or later.
There's no version for Intel Macs, older macOS, Windows or Linux.

cards.title: A tab switcher you hold Control-Tab for
steps: Ode has no tab switcher panel. Control-Tab jumps straight to the tab you used last.
To pick from your recent tabs, open the Command Bar: Recent Tabs show before you type.

cards.title: Previews for Outlook, Notion and other sites
steps: Tab previews work for Gmail and Google Calendar only.
Other sites, such as Outlook, show no preview yet.

cards.title: Show only the page in full screen
steps: Choose View > Enter Full Screen.
The sidebar hides and the page fills the screen. Move the pointer to the edge to see it.
cards.waitsFor: Full-screen behavior. Confirm what full screen hides and how the sidebar comes back, then merge this card into full-screen.

cards.title: Open a site as its own app
questions: open gmail in its own window
steps: Right-click the pinned tab and choose Open as App.
The site opens in its own window, with its own Dock icon and no sidebar.
cards.waitsFor: App windows. Confirm the command's name, where it is offered, and which Space's sign-ins the window uses.

cards.title: Limit time on distracting sites
steps: Click Site Controls on the site and set a daily limit.
When you reach it, Ode covers the page until the next day.
cards.waitsFor: Focus tools. Confirm where limits are set, what happens at the limit, and how to override it.

cards.title: Hide feeds, Shorts and recommendations
steps: Click Site Controls on YouTube or another supported site.
Turn on the focus preset to hide its feed, Shorts and suggestions.
cards.waitsFor: Focus presets. Confirm the supported sites and the control's name. Until then, Zap in a Boost hides these by hand.

cards.title: Fill passwords from your password manager on every page
steps: Install the password manager's extension in each Space.
On WebKit pages, choose the password from the AutoFill list when you click a sign-in field.
cards.waitsFor: Password managers proven on every page. Confirm which managers fill and save on Chromium and WebKit pages, then fold the result into password-manager-extension.

cards.title: Sync your Spaces and tabs between Macs
questions: set up sync on my other mac
steps: Choose Ode > Settings, then click Sync.
Turn on Sync with iCloud on each Mac signed in to the same Apple Account.
If Ode asks which copy to keep, choose Use This Device or Use iCloud.
cards.waitsFor: Apple's approval of Ode's iCloud container. When sync ships, make this live and retire the sync-between-macs card.
